open_decisions.D17: sig_policy algorithm-ID numeric values — proposed 0=ed25519, 1=ml-dsa-65, 2-15 reserved; ratified in code at M0 wave 3, formal flip at Q14

resolved_decisions.D9: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — GGM node address = (level, index) uint pair (candidate A); docs/decisions/D9-ggm-node-address.md. Former pending-D9 items now carry `proposed`.
resolved_decisions.D23: RESOLVED 2026-07-27 — a file's raw mirror is that file's last unit; at most one per file. Seal-side construction rule; parse position-agnostic.
resolved_decisions.D28: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — full-reveal strictness is STRICT (hard-fail): a bundle revealing every kind=Normal unit of a file MUST carry that file's file_salt, plus s_root iff the file has a fine tree. Rider 1 (binding on F8): reveal shape is DERIVED from the signed unit table and the revealed set, NEVER declared — the bundle carries no reveal-shape discriminant. docs/decisions/D28-full-reveal-strictness.md
resolved_decisions.D77: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — a zero-non-mirror-unit (mirror-only) file is REJECTED at F5 (manifest schema), code manifest-empty-normal-units via ContainerField::NormalUnits, checked in FileEntry::new AFTER the units.is_empty() check and BEFORE the coverage loop. This DOES change the registry, correcting the fed_but_not_resolved_here note that assumed otherwise: maps.file_entry key 6 gains 'at least one kind=normal unit [P]'. D28's anti-vacuity clause and C7's attest refusal stay as defence-in-depth (R's view types are hand-populated, so no F5 check can constrain them). docs/decisions/D77-zero-unit-file.md
resolved_decisions.D10: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — 19 frozen parser resource caps, one universal clamp rule min(claimed_length, remaining_input) applied at every pre-allocation whether or not a cap covers it, 18 new bundle-/manifest- codes plus the existing cbor-nesting-too-deep; all enforced inside verify stage 1 (decode), ahead of every AEAD, hash and signature operation; u64 everywhere so wasm32 and native cannot diverge. Mirrored in the top-level `caps` object and in registry-v1.md section 11. docs/decisions/D10-parser-caps.md

validation_tiers.proposed_rule: bundle schema validation never consults the embedded manifest (D8 feed item 8)

tiers.decidable_from: bundle plus embedded manifest, or crypto

decode_layers.zero_copy_requirement: layer 2 must receive a sub-slice of the bundle input, never a copy: Manifest's guarantee that work_id and signature pre-images are the received bytes holds by construction only for a borrowed slice

max_container_depth.cap_basis: max of the two, not the sum — layer 2 starts a fresh decoder over the bstr contents
max_container_depth.note: cap frozen by D10 as MAX_CBOR_DEPTH = 8 = 6 + 2, leaving room for one additive v1.x field nested one level deeper; see the top-level `caps` object

discriminants.read_after: nothing — first key of the file

version_dispatch.envelope_frozen_across_versions: the manifest body's discriminant sits INSIDE the body bstr, so the {body, signatures} envelope must be parsed before the version is readable at all; it therefore can never carry a version-specific change, and has no reserved band and no discriminant of its own (§1 rule 6, §7.1)
version_dispatch.discriminants_are_independent: a v1 bundle may one day carry a v2 manifest; the two rejections are separate codes in separate families (D78) and must stay separable
version_dispatch.unsupported_is_not_malformed: an unrowed version yields the version error and NOTHING else — never a canonicality error and never an unknown/reserved-key error, even when the rest of the artifact would also fail v1 validation. A *missing* discriminant is `*-missing-key`; a non-canonical one is the `cbor-*` class.
version_dispatch.constant_cost_peek: canonical maps ascend (§1 rule 3), so key 0 is first on the wire whenever present and the version peek is constant-cost in artifact size — an unsupported oversized artifact is rejected before any section is walked, earlier than the F11 caps apply
version_dispatch.released_versions_decodable_forever: MVP-SPEC.md line 123: support is added by appending a row to the dispatch table, never by widening an older version's decoder

checked_absences.note: F8's checklist test asserts these are absent, rather than merely not implementing them

items.reason: nonces come from the manifest — single source of truth (MVP-SPEC.md line 114)

items.absent: any signature container at bundle level
items.reason: the bundle is unsigned; authority is the embedded signed manifest plus the anchor artifacts. Signing the bundle would invite trusting the assembler, who is the sealer (line 121)

items.absent: work_id / anchor_digest / seal_id at bundle level
items.reason: all derived; a stored copy could contradict the bytes it summarizes
positional — bundle key 3 is OTS, key 4 is TSA (section 7.6.2); the illegal cross-placement is unrepresentable

items.absent: any reveal-shape discriminant (is_full_reveal, reveal_mode, reveal_shape) at any level
items.reason: D28 rider 1 — reveal shape is DERIVED from the signed unit table and the revealed set. A declared shape is sealer-forgeable: declaring 'partial' while revealing every unit would smuggle back the permissive full-reveal option D28 rejected. BINDING CONSTRAINT ON F8 — do not add this field

profile.encoding: RFC 8949 section 4.2.1 Core Deterministic (MVP-SPEC.md line 73; minicbor =2.3.0 per D7)
profile.key_error_bands: unassigned key in 0..=23 -> reserved-slot error naming the key; key >= 24 -> unknown-key error (F10)
profile.magic_bytes: none — version discriminant is map key 0, first in canonical encoded order

caps.enforcement_point: verify stage 1 (decode) — every cap fires before any AEAD, hash, or signature work
caps.wasm32_parity: every byte/count cap is u64 and <= u32::MAX, so each is reachable and compares identically on wasm32 and native; MAX_CBOR_DEPTH is the deliberate u16 exception (it counts containers, never wire lengths)
caps.clamp_rule: every pre-allocation clamped to min(claimed_length, remaining_input); order at an array head is head canonicality -> cap -> clamped allocation -> elements
caps.recorded_non_caps: sig_policy / pubkeys / signatures (bounded by the 16-value registered sig_alg universe of section 6.2 and by duplicate-freedom, so an existing code fires first); range / cover_entry / path_node (fixed arity); title / app_version / touched_file.path / tsa_anchor.source (free-form tstr, transitively bounded by caps 1-2); revealed-unit ciphertext (already shape-checked; an upper bound would equal MAX_BUNDLE_BYTES). The clamp rule still applies to every one of them.
caps.not_in_scope: internal structural limits of the opaque artifacts (.ots op counts, DER nesting, signed-attribute counts) are A's at M2 (sections 7.8, 7.9; MVP-SPEC.md line 153) — their freeze status is decision D83

R and not X because a unit's OWNING FILE is a manifest fact — the unit table is nested inside file entries — which D78 forbids the bundle schema layer from reaching for; so it is a verify-pipeline outcome, not a bundle- code, and R4/R5 mints the final spelling. Evidence: line 95 (path_salt ships whenever any reveal TOUCHES the file, so the recipient can verify the path) and line 121 (only two rendering states: revealed content, or unrevealed files as placeholders with path withheld). Rider: the two routes to fine_root must be required to AGREE (open tamper row for R4/Q8)

fields.name: path

maps.name: full_reveal
maps.doc: MVP-SPEC.md lines 112-114/121 per fully-revealed file. D28 (resolved 2026-07-28) makes this section's presence a BICONDITIONAL over a DERIVED predicate, not a sealer option: an entry exists for file F iff full(F). The entry is material, not a claim — its presence must AGREE with the independently derived predicate, and there is no reveal-shape field anywhere to declare it
